To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the synthesis of [14 c]4-acetyl-phenylalanin was successfully achieved, the cell viability and incorporation of [14 C]-4-acetylphenylanine into endogenous proteins in male rat hepatocyte cultures was determined, and the results showed that there is no evidence of carbon 14 incorporation into hepatocytes endogenous proteins with 14 C-4-acetyl- phenylalanine and there is no difference between it, and L-phenyalanine in cell viability assessments.
[14 C]acetic anhydride, 1 was prepared in a one-step radiochemical synthesis from [1- 14 C]acrylic acid, 2 in a 60% radiochemical yield.
[14 C]AcF, 4 was synthesized in two chemical steps from [1 14 C]acetylene chloride in an 8% radio chemical yield and 99.9 radio chemical purity.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the synthesis, biological evaluation and assessment of the incorporation into proteins of 4-acetyl-L-phenylalanin.
the development of a novel, stable, biodegradable, and bioactive peptide drug delivery system for the delivery of a therapeutic protein.
the synthesis of [14C]4-acetyl-L-phenylalanin, 4-acetyl-L-phe, 4, and its incorporation into proteins.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
there was no incorporation of 14C-acetylphenyl alanine into endogenous proteins of male rat hepatocytes and no evidence of cytotoxicity at any of the tested concentrations of [14 C(U) pAcF.
there is no evidence that [14 C] pAcF, 4 is incorporated into endogenous rat liver proteins or that it has any effect on cell viability.
the [14 C]acetylated phenylalanine, [14 C] pAcF, does not cause any adverse effects on cell viability and is not incorporated into endogenous protein in primary male rat hepatocyte cultures.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the incorporation of 4-acetyl-phenylalanin-14 C into endogenous proteins is not likely to occur at concentrations of 4-acetylated-phenylalan-14 C that are likely to be encountered during the in vitro studies of protein PEGylation.
the incorporation of [14 C]-4-acetylphenylanine, 4, into endogenous proteins in primary male rat hepatocyte cultures does not occur at concentrations up to 1 mM.

[14 C] pAcF, 4 can be synthesized in a 2 step process from [1- 14 C]acety chloride in an overall yield of 8% and in 99% radiochemical purity and that there is no evidence of carbon 14 incorporation into endogenous rat liver proteins.
The main takeaway from our work is that
4-acetyl-phenylalanin is not toxic to cells and does not incorporate into proteins in hepatocytes.
the incorporation of [14 C]-4-acetylphenylanine into proteins in primary rat hepatocytes is negligible and that the cell viability of hepatocytes is not affected by 4-acetyl-phenylalanin
[14 C]AcF is an effective and stable amino acid that can be used in in vitro studies without the need for a metabolic block.
